correctness.rationale: Proof: complete-bipartite forest complex decomposes into two contractible cones intersecting in a complete bipartite graph. The integral second homology identifies with its fundamental-cycle lattice. A missing graph edge supplies tetrahedra whose boundaries are the fundamental square-cycle basis; they kill all integral H2, while the common two-skeleton gives simple connectivity. One deletion adds precisely the basis tetrahedra, hence contractibility via the relative cellular sequence and Whitehead. Two disjoint deletions in K3,3 have f-vector (1,6,15,20,13,2), two independent primitive top boundaries and integral H3=Z, hence homotopy S3. Independent tests exhaust 848 labelled bipartite graph profiles and 51,456 vertex subsets, check 120 additional larger profiles and all 79 single-edge deletions in the selected sizes; mod-two ranks corroborate, not substitute for integral arguments.

originality.rationale: The complete-bipartite wedge formula and girth bound are known from Carnero Bravo (arXiv:2307.13271). The claimed new contribution is the global proper-bipartite 2-connectivity dichotomy, the contractible one-deletion boundary, and a sharp two-deletion S3 case. The published girth inequality is strictly weaker on proper bipartite graphs of girth four. Both relevant 2023 full-text sections and the published-record query results were compared by implication, not keyword or title alone.

value.rationale: A sharp, universally quantified topology threshold for the induced-forest complexes of bipartite graphs. An arbitrarily large free H2 survives only in the complete biclique; deleting one edge removes all of it and produces a contractible space. The new connectivity statement covers every graph of girth four with a missing cross-edge, sharpening the earlier girth bound by one dimension; deleting two independent edges already makes genuine H3, proving sharpness and motivating further study of the first higher homology.
